theming.firstPaint.body: Without help, a reload shows the theme that the operating system prefers until React renders. themeScript returns the text of an inline script that sets the stored theme before the first paint. This is what it returns for the key of the example:
theming.firstPaint.rules: It has to use the same storageKey as the store, and it has to be in the HTML that is served, in the head: a script that React renders does not run.
theming.firstPaint.title: First paint
theming.lead: Light, dark and system: how your application owns the choice, from the first paint to the provider.
theming.modes.body: tokens.css paints the light theme and follows prefers-color-scheme until a theme is chosen. The data-theme attribute on the html element overrides it: light and dark set it, and system removes it.
theming.modes.title: Light, dark and system
theming.modes.try: Try it. The buttons set the preference of this site, the one that the theme switcher of the top bar shows.
theming.next.body: The theme changes the colors, not what a component asks of you. Read what each one needs for keyboard, focus and labels.
theming.next.title: Check the accessibility obligations
theming.persistence.memory: When storage is unavailable (private mode, or blocked), the choice lasts in memory, for that store only.
theming.persistence.storage: The choice is kept in localStorage under the key you pass. A stored value that is not light or dark counts as system.
theming.persistence.sync: While a component reads the store, it follows the other tabs and the operating system switching between light and dark.
theming.persistence.title: Persistence
theming.provider.body: FormaProvider is about text, not about theme: it replaces the strings that the components show on their own. The theme works with or without it, so the toggle can go anywhere in your application.
theming.provider.title: With the provider
theming.store.body: createThemeStore creates the store of one application: it keeps the preference under your key, and creating it does not touch the page. useTheme reads it in a component and returns preference, resolved, setPreference and toggle.
theming.store.resolved: preference is what the person chose, and resolved is what is painted: while the preference is system, it follows the operating system.
theming.store.title: The preference store
